what: Frontline owns one of the world's largest fleets of crude oil tankers, including very large carriers, and earns money by hauling oil between producers and refineries at whatever the market rate is.
customers: Oil producers, traders and refiners chartering tankers, on spot voyages and time charters.
money: very large crude carriers on long-haul routes
moat: A large modern fleet that cannot be expanded quickly: a new tanker takes three years to build, so when rates rise there is no way to add supply in time.
risks: Tanker rates are extremely volatile and the company has no control over them
$3.1B of debt against $251M of cash in a cyclical business
Only four analysts cover the stock
opportunities: 6.7 times earnings with a 19.2% net margin and $689M of free cash flow
Longer shipping routes caused by sanctions and rerouting keep more tankers busy for the same barrels
watch: Average daily tanker rates and the order book for new tankers worldwide.
